request.spec:
The sheet's settings assign a role to a user name: clerk (the default for any name) or steward
(ROLE_SET user=<name> role=<role>). The sheet also has a clerk limit (two decimals; blank means no
limit; SETTING_CHANGED key=clerk-limit value=<limit>). A clerk can settle a claim only when its
due is at or below the limit; above it, settling is refused with an error on the claim. A claim
whose due is n/a is within any limit. Stewards settle anything. The opener still cannot settle
their own claim.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The sheet's settings assign a role to a user name: clerk (the default for any name) or steward
(ROLE_SET user=<name> role=<role>). The sheet also has a clerk limit (two decimals; blank means no
limit; SETTING_CHANGED key=clerk-limit value=<limit>). A clerk can settle a claim only when its
due is at or below the limit; above it, settling is refused with an error on the claim. A claim
whose due is n/a is within any limit. Stewards settle anything. The opener still cannot settle
their own claim.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Roles and the clerk limit are in, and all 4 acceptance scenarios pass on the first `bin/e2e` run.

**How settling works now**
- A clerk can settle a claim only if its due is at or below the sheet's clerk limit. Above the limit, the server refuses and the claim row shows the error.
- A claim whose due is n/a is always within the limit.
- Stewards can settle anything.
- The opener still can't settle their own claim; that check runs before the limit check.

**Stored data:** a new migration, `V18__settings.sql`, adds a nullable `clerk_limit` column to `sheet` (blank means no limit) and a `sheet_role` table. Any name without a row there is a clerk.

**Server:** a new `settings` package with three endpoints:
- `GET /api/sheets/{id}/settings`
- `POST /api/sheets/{id}/settings` sets the clerk limit, which must be blank or 0.00 or more with up to two decimals. It writes `SETTING_CHANGED … key=clerk-limit value=<limit>`, even when the value hasn't changed — the test expects that.
- `POST /api/sheets/{id}/roles` assigns a role. Anything other than `clerk` or `steward` (e.g. `boss`) is refused. It writes `ROLE_SET … user=<name> role=<role>`.

The limit check itself is in `ChangeClaimStatus.java`.

**Front end:** a new settings panel in `features/settings/` has:
- the clerk-limit form, showing the limit currently in force
- the role form
- a list of the roles set, using the `data-testid` names the test expects

The test helper fills an optional "from" date field for a setting if the screen has one. I left that field out because the request doesn't call for dated settings, so the limit always applies from the moment it's saved.
